  PROBLEM: verify_token() accepts either GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN, but the three Stage 2 diagnostic messages hardcode "GH_TOKEN", misdirecting operators when only GITHUB_TOKEN is set.
  WHY: The probe logic is correct, but the operator-facing diagnostics name an environment variable that may be absent.

  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The REST identity probe unconditionally invokes `timeout 15 gh api user` without checking whether the `timeout` binary is available.
  WHY: On hosts without `timeout`, the probe fails before contacting the network and emits a misleading authentication warning even when `gh api user` would succeed unwrapped; severity was reported as MAJOR by minimax_minimax-m3 and NIT by the other reviewers.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh
  Line or code reference: 179, 184, 187 (and byte-identical lines in workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/session-start.sh)
  Problem: verify_token() accepts either GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN (line 131 checks both), but the three case-branch messages mention only "GH_TOKEN" by name.
  Why it fails at runtime: The probe itself works correctly regardless of which token variable is set. The failure is operational: a human reading the session-start log when only GITHUB_TOKEN is configured sees messages about GH_TOKEN and may waste time checking or re-setting the wrong variable.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh
  Line or code reference: 154 (and byte-identical line in workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/session-start.sh)
  Problem: The REST identity probe on line 154 unconditionally wraps gh api user with timeout 15, but does not guard the timeout binary with command -v.
  Why it fails at runtime: The entrypoint main() on line 219 gates verify_token() behind CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true, which is only true in Claude Code Web sessions that run in Linux containers where coreutils timeout is always present. So this cannot fail in any currently supported environment. It becomes a real failure path only if the guard on line 219 is ever widened to include local macOS sessions.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2

=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 179, 184, 187 (Stage 2 `case` branches; byte-identical mirror at workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/session-start.sh:179, 184, 187)
  Problem: verify_token() accepts either GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN (the entry guard at line 131 is `[ -z "${GH_TOKEN:-}" ] && [ -z "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]`), but the three new branch messages hardcode the literal string "GH_TOKEN".
  Why it fails at runtime: every CLI/Web session where GITHUB_TOKEN is the only token set will see "does NOT forward GH_TOKEN" / "does not prove GH_TOKEN was forwarded" / "cannot determine whether GH_TOKEN or an agent-proxy credential authenticated the request", even though no GH_TOKEN exists in the session.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh
  Line or code reference: line 154 (`if ! gh_login=$(timeout 15 gh api user --jq .login 2>/dev/null) || [ -z "${gh_login}" ]; then`; byte-identical mirror at workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/session-start.sh:154)
  Problem: the LAST RUN DIFF wrapped the REST identity probe in `timeout 15` but added no `command -v timeout` guard.
  Why it fails at runtime: any session host without coreutils `timeout` (macOS local CLI, minimal containers, hardened runners) fails the identity probe unconditionally on the first subprocess, before the network is ever contacted.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh (and the byte-identical workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/session-start.sh mirror)
  Location: line 154 (and matching line in template mirror)
  Issue: asymmetric `command -v` guarding. `gh` and `curl` are guarded; `timeout` is not.
  Suggested minimal fix: guard the wrapper or capture the timeout binary into a local with a sensible fallback; add a test case for `timeout` absent from PATH.
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3

- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh (and the byte-identical workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/session-start.sh mirror)
  Location: lines 179, 184, 187 (the three Stage 2 NOTE branches)
  Issue: the branch messages name only "GH_TOKEN" even though verify_token accepts either env var.
  Suggested minimal fix: replace the literal "GH_TOKEN" with a short phrase that names both accepted env vars.
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k3 ===
- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh (and byte-identical workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/session-start.sh)
  Line or code reference: line 131 (`if [ -z "${GH_TOKEN:-}" ] && [ -z "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]`) versus the stage-2 messages at lines 179, 184, and 187
  Problem: verify_token() accepts either GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN, and CLAUDE.md §23.G explicitly documents GITHUB_TOKEN as an accepted fallback name, but all three new stage-2 NOTE messages hard-code "GH_TOKEN".
  Why it fails at runtime: in a session that sets only GITHUB_TOKEN, every stage-2 diagnostic names a variable that is not set, misdirecting the operator's debugging toward the wrong env var.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh (and byte-identical workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/session-start.sh)
  Line or code reference: line 154 (`if ! gh_login=$(timeout 15 gh api user --jq .login 2>/dev/null) || [ -z "${gh_login}" ]`)
  Problem: the REST identity probe now hard-depends on the `timeout` binary with no availability guard.
  Why it fails at runtime: If `timeout` is absent, the probe fails with command-not-found, gh_login stays empty, and the hook emits the WARNING "GitHub authentication is unavailable or api.github.com could not be reached" even when `gh api user` would have succeeded unwrapped.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2

- file: .claude/hooks/session-start.sh
  location: line 154
  issue: unguarded `timeout` dependency
  suggested minimal fix: wrap the probe as `if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then gh_probe=(timeout 15 gh api user --jq .login); else gh_probe=(gh api user --jq .login); fi` and invoke `"${gh_probe[@]}"`.
  estimated lines changed: 4

- file: .claude/hooks/session-start.sh
  location: lines 179, 184, 187 (and the same lines in the workflow-templates mirror)
  issue: the branch messages name only "GH_TOKEN" even though verify_token accepts either env var.
  suggested minimal fix: replace the literal "GH_TOKEN" with a short phrase that names both accepted env vars.
  estimated lines changed: 3-6 (hook), plus 3-6 (template mirror); no test change required.

- file: .claude/hooks/session-start.sh
  location: lines 179, 184, 187
  issue: `gh_login` is taken from a network response and interpolated directly into log lines; a CR/LF or control-character payload would forge additional `[session-start]` lines in the session transcript.
  suggested minimal fix: sanitize once after the probe, e.g. `gh_login=$(printf '%s' "${gh_login}" | tr -d '\r\n')`.
  estimated lines changed: 1
